# Who Takes Part

<!-- STEP id="nodes" -->
Four kinds of players take part in an economy: **consumers** who buy, **producers** who make and sell, the **government**, and **financial institutions** such as banks. The book calls them **economic entities**.

<!-- STEP id="flows" -->
They pass money to each other all the time. Producers pay wages to workers. Consumers pay prices for goods. People and firms pay taxes to the government. Banks give loans.

<!-- STEP id="economy" -->
All of this together is the **economy**: how a country or region produces, trades and uses goods and services, and how money moves. Economics studies it: how people earn wages, how prices are set, how wealth is shared, and how trade and government policy change prices and jobs.
